e-4765.knowledge_point: Finding the LU Factorization of a 2x2 Matrix
e-4765.worked_solution:
To find the matrices $L$ and $U,$ we reduce the matrix $A$ to row echelon form. Whilst doing this, we simultaneously write down the row operations applied to $A$ in terms of matrix multiplication using elementary matrices.

$$
\begin{aligned}A & =[\begin{aligned}7 & 9 \\ -7 & -6\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+1\cdot {R}_{1}\,⟺\,\overset{{E}_{1}}{\overset{⏞}{[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 1 & 1\end{aligned}]}}\cdot A \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}7 & 9 \\ 0 & 3\end{aligned}] \\  & =U\end{aligned}
$$

The reduced matrix is upper triangular, so it is our matrix $U.$ Now, since $E_1A=U,$ we can invert $E_1$ to arrive at the desired LU factorization:

$$
\begin{aligned}{E}_{1}A & =U \\ A & ={E}_{1}^{-1}U \\ A & ={[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 1 & 1\end{aligned}]}^{-1}U \\ A & ={{[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ -1 & 1\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{L}{{[\begin{aligned}7 & 9 \\ 0 & 3\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{U}\end{aligned}
$$

content.worked_solution:
To find the matrices $L$ and $U,$ we reduce the matrix $B$ to row echelon form. Whilst doing this, we simultaneously write down the row operations applied to $B$ in terms of matrix multiplication using elementary matrices:

$$
\begin{aligned}B & =[\begin{aligned}3 & 9 \\ 7 & 20\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+(-\frac{7}{3}){R}_{1}\,⟺\,\overset{{E}_{1}}{\overset{⏞}{[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ -\frac{7}{3} & 1\end{aligned}]}}\cdot B \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}3 & 9 \\ 0 & -1\end{aligned}] \\  & =U\end{aligned}
$$

The reduced matrix is upper triangular, so it is our matrix $U.$ Now, since ${E}_{1}B=U,$ we can invert ${E}_{1}$ to arrive at the desired LU factorization:

$$
\begin{aligned}{E}_{1}B & =U \\ B & ={E}_{1}^{-1}U \\ B & ={[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ -\frac{7}{3} & 1\end{aligned}]}^{-1}U \\ B & ={{[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ \frac{7}{3} & 1\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{L}{{[\begin{aligned}3 & 9 \\ 0 & -1\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{U}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, ${l}_{21}=\frac{7}{3},{u}_{12}=9,$ and ${l}_{21}\cdot {u}_{12}=21.$

content.worked_solution:
To find the matrices $L$ and $U,$ we reduce the matrix $A$ to row echelon form. Whilst doing this, we simultaneously write down the row operations applied to $A$ in terms of matrix multiplication using elementary matrices:

$$
\begin{aligned}A & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 5 \\ -5 & -7\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+5{R}_{1}\,⟺\,\overset{{E}_{1}}{\overset{⏞}{[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 5 & 1\end{aligned}]}}\cdot D \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 5 \\ 0 & 18\end{aligned}] \\  & =U\end{aligned}
$$

The reduced matrix is upper triangular, so it is our matrix $U.$ Now, since ${E}_{1}A=U,$ we can invert ${E}_{1}$ to arrive at the desired LU factorization:

$$
\begin{aligned}{E}_{1}A & =U \\ A & ={E}_{1}^{-1}U \\ A & ={[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 5 & 1\end{aligned}]}^{-1}U \\ A & ={{[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ -5 & 1\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{L}{{[\begin{aligned}1 & 5 \\ 0 & 18\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{U}\end{aligned}
$$

Given that $A=[\begin{aligned}-3 & -2 \\ 9 & 6\end{aligned}]$
has the LU decomposition $A=LU$, then ${l}_{21}+{u}_{22}=$
content.worked_solution:
To find the matrices $L$ and $U,$ we reduce the matrix $A$ to row echelon form. Whilst doing this, we simultaneously write down the row operations applied to $A$ in terms of matrix multiplication using elementary matrices:

$$
\begin{aligned}A & =[\begin{aligned}-3 & -2 \\ 9 & 6\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+3{R}_{1}\,⟺\,\overset{{E}_{1}}{\overset{⏞}{[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 3 & 1\end{aligned}]}}\cdot A \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}-3 & -2 \\ 0 & 0\end{aligned}] \\  & =U\end{aligned}
$$

The reduced matrix is upper triangular, so it is our matrix $U.$ Now, since ${E}_{1}A=U,$ we can invert ${E}_{1}$ to arrive at the desired LU factorization:

$$
\begin{aligned}{E}_{1}A & =U \\ A & ={E}_{1}^{-1}U \\ A & ={[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 3 & 1\end{aligned}]}^{-1}U \\ A & ={{[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ -3 & 1\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{L}{{[\begin{aligned}-3 & -2 \\ 0 & 0\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{U}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, ${l}_{21}=-3,{u}_{22}=0,$ and ${l}_{21}+{u}_{22}=-3.$

after.problem:
Given that
$A=[\begin{aligned}4 & -1 \\ 12 & -3\end{aligned}]$
has the LU decomposition $A=LU$, then ${l}_{21}+{u}_{22}=$
after.worked_solution:
To find the matrices $L$ and $U,$ we reduce the matrix $A$ to row echelon form. Whilst doing this, we simultaneously write down the row operations applied to $A$ in terms of matrix multiplication using elementary matrices:

$$
\begin{aligned}A & =[\begin{aligned}4 & -1 \\ 12 & -3\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+(-3){R}_{1}\,⟺\,\overset{{E}_{1}}{\overset{⏞}{[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ -3 & 1\end{aligned}]}}\cdot A \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}4 & -1 \\ 0 & 0\end{aligned}] \\  & =U\end{aligned}
$$

The reduced matrix is upper triangular, so it is our matrix $U.$ Now, since ${E}_{1}A=U,$ we can invert ${E}_{1}$ to arrive at the desired LU factorization:

$$
\begin{aligned}{E}_{1}A & =U \\ A & ={E}_{1}^{-1}U \\ A & ={[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ -3 & 1\end{aligned}]}^{-1}U \\ A & ={{[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 3 & 1\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{L}{{[\begin{aligned}4 & -1 \\ 0 & 0\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{U}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, ${l}_{21}=3,$ ${u}_{22}=0,$ and ${l}_{21}+{u}_{22}=3.$
